questions.question:
Given below are four statements.

Statement 1: All students are inquisitive.
Statement 2: Some students are inquisitive.
Statement 3: No student is inquisitive.
Statement 4: Some students are not inquisitive.

From the given four statements, find the two statements that CANNOT BE TRUE simultaneously, assuming that there is at least one student in the class.
questions.explanation:
"All students are inquisitive" and "No student is inquisitive" directly contradict each other (there is at least one student), so they can never both be true.

Every other pair can hold together (e.g. statements 2 and 4 hold when some are and some are not inquisitive).

Answer: Statement 1 and Statement 3

A survey for a certain year found that 90% of pregnant women received medical care at least once before giving birth. Of these women, 60% received medical care from doctors, while 40% received medical care from other healthcare providers.

doctor.
options.B:
Less than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a
doctor.
options.C:
More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at most once from a
doctor.

questions.question: In a college, there are three student clubs, 60 students are only in the Drama club, 80 students are only in the Dance club, 30 students are only in Maths club, 40 students are in both Drama and Dance clubs, 12 students are in both Dance and Maths clubs, 7 students are in both Drama and Maths clubs, and 2 students are in all clubs. If 75% of the students in the college are not in any of these clubs, then the total number of students in the college is _____.
questions.explanation:
The "both" counts include the 2 students in all three clubs, so the exactly-two counts are 38, 10 and 5.

Students in clubs = 60 + 80 + 30 (only one) + 38 + 10 + 5 (exactly two) + 2 (all three) = 225.

These are 25% of the college, so total = 225 / 0.25 = 900.

Answer: 900

questions.question:
The diagram below shows a river system consisting of 7 segments, marked P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V. It splits the land into 5 zones, marked Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z5. We need to connect these zones using the least number of bridges. Out of the following options, which one is correct?
Note: The figure shown is representative.

options.A: Bridges on P, Q, and T
options.B: Bridges on P, Q, S, and T
options.C: Bridges on Q, R, T, and V
options.D: Bridges on P, Q, S, U, and V

questions.explanation:
This problem can be solved by representing the map as a graph:

- Each zone is represented as a vertex. - Each river segment where a bridge can be built is represented as an edge connecting the adjacent zones.

The graph is as follows:

River Segment Adjacent Zones
P Z1- Z2
Q Z1- Z3
R Z2- Z3
S Z1- Z5
T Z3- Z5
U Z5- Z4
V Z3- Z4

We have 5 vertices (zones). To connect all zones with the minimum number of bridges, we need a spanning tree, which always contains

[latex] n-1=5-1=4 [/latex] edges.

Now check each option.

Option A: Bridges on P, Q, and T
Only 3 bridges are used, so all 5 zones cannot be connected.
Incorrect.

Option B: Bridges on P, Q, S, and T
The selected edges are:
- P : Z1-Z2 - Q : Z1-Z3 - S : Z1-Z5 - T : Z3-Z5

Zone Z4 is not connected.
Incorrect.

Option C: Bridges on Q, R, T, and V
The selected edges are:
- Q : Z1-Z3 - R : Z2-Z3 - T : Z3-Z5 - V : Z3-Z4

Every zone is connected, and there are exactly 4 bridges (forming a spanning tree).
Correct.

Option D: Bridges on P, Q, S, U, and V
Uses 5 bridges, whereas only 4 are required for a minimum spanning connection.
Incorrect.
